introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).

Le corrigé traite brièvement les quatre pour que le candidat puisse en retenir trois. Aucun point n'est imprimé par sous-partie, seulement « (25 marks) » en fin de liste.
Neutralité : les croyances sont présentées comme celles des musulmans (« Muslims believe », « according to Islamic tradition ») ; aucun numéro de sourate ni de hadith n'est cité.

Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY ». Cette règle (4 questions d'UNE SEULE section) n'est pas exprimable avec `parmi` (un seul groupe) ni `ou` (sous-questions) : `regles_choix` reste vide dans tous les fichiers et la consigne complète est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source ; les références sont limitées à des passages et faits bien établis, les autres points sont formulés prudemment (« according to Islamic tradition », « Muslims believe »). À faire relire par un spécialiste des études religieuses avant mise en avant.

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the Islamic teaching on any three of the following?

(a) Love

(b) Peace

(c) Education

(d) Solidarity

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Islam teaches that faith must be expressed in relationships with others. A candidate answers any three of the four topics; they are all presented below, and any three would obtain full marks.

**(a) Love.**
- Islam teaches first the love of God, which is the highest form of love: the believer loves God above all else and shows it by obedience and gratitude. God is described as Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim (the Compassionate and the Merciful), and Muslims are urged to imitate this mercy.
- Love for others: the Prophet Muhammad is described in the Qur'an as a mercy to the worlds. A well-known saying attributed to him states that none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
- This love is expressed in practical forms: kindness to parents, care of relatives, neighbours, orphans and the poor, hospitality, forgiveness and honesty. Muslims are also taught to be just even towards those they dislike.
- Love of the Prophet and of the believers is part of faith; but Islam links love with justice and obedience to God.

**(b) Peace.**
- The word "Islam" comes from the same root as salam (peace), and means submission to God, through which one finds peace. Muslims greet each other with "as-salamu alaykum" (peace be upon you), and the Qur'an calls Paradise "the abode of peace".
- Islam teaches peace within oneself (through faith and prayer), in the family, in society and between nations. It forbids aggression, the unjust killing of the innocent and corruption on earth, and encourages forgiveness and reconciliation. Disputes should be settled by justice and, if possible, by mediation.
- War is permitted only under strict conditions, such as defence against aggression, and the Qur'an urges accepting peace if the enemy inclines to it. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (628 CE), in which the Prophet accepted terms that seemed unfavourable in order to secure peace, is often cited as an example.

**(c) Education.**
- The first word revealed to the Prophet was "Iqra'" ("Read" or "Recite"). Seeking knowledge is regarded as an obligation on every Muslim, men and women alike, according to a saying widely quoted in the tradition.
- Education is both religious (the Qur'an, the Sunnah, law) and worldly (medicine, mathematics, astronomy, trade). In early Islamic history this produced centres of learning such as the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, and institutions such as al-Azhar in Cairo; Muslim scholars contributed to medicine, mathematics, optics and other fields.
- According to tradition, some prisoners taken after the battle of Badr were released after teaching reading to Muslim children. Education brings people closer to God, helps them to serve society and fights ignorance and poverty.

**(d) Solidarity.**
- Muslims are taught that the believers are like one body: when one part suffers, the whole body feels it. The Qur'an calls the believers brothers.
- Practical forms include zakat (the compulsory alms), voluntary charity (sadaqah), endowments (waqf), care for the poor, orphans, travellers and debtors, and the Prophet's brotherhood between the Muhajirun (emigrants from Makkah) and the Ansar (helpers of Madinah).
- Rituals strengthen solidarity: congregational prayer, the fast in Ramadan, which makes the rich feel hunger, and the hajj, where all pilgrims wear simple clothing and stand together at Arafat.

**Conclusion.** Islam teaches that love of God and of people, peace, the pursuit of knowledge and solidarity are central moral duties, based on the Qur'an and the example of the Prophet, and that they should shape both personal behaviour and the life of the community.
